transcript.content: Hello. I am Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It is very nice to meet you. Thank you for taking the time to see me. 

I hope I'm explaining this right... I'm mostly just here because, well, I guess I've been having a little bit of trouble communicating at work lately. It's probably nothing terrible, I'm sure it's just stress or something, but I'm a retail supervisor, and when I try to explain the inventory numbers, or just go over the weekend schedule with my team... my words start sort of jumping around a bit. 

Like, I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then suddenly I'm talking about Thursdays, and then the church grill, and then maybe my boss's tone of voice. And, well, people look at me like they can't really follow what I'm saying. It's a little embarrassing, to be honest, because I really try to be clear for them. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and making sense. Does that make sense to you? Is that okay to start with?
Beyond the difficulty with your speech, have you been seeing or hearing things that others around you do not seem to notice?

Oh, no, Dr. Smith. No, I haven't noticed anything like that at all. I mean, my hearing isn't quite what it was when I was younger, but... no, I'm definitely not hearing voices or seeing anything unusual. It's really just that embarrassment with my words getting all tangled up when I talk to my team. 

I haven't had any of those other things happen. I hope that's a good sign? I mean, that's a positive thing, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, such as frequent headaches, dizziness, or numbness in any part of your body lately?

Oh, no, nothing like that. No headaches or... or dizziness, or anything going numb. I've been very lucky there. Physically, I feel pretty good, actually. I mean, just the normal tiredness from being on my feet on the sales floor at my age, but definitely nothing out of the ordinary. 

I hope that's helpful? I'm trying to give you the best picture I can. Is it okay that I don't have any of those physical symptoms to report? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you what you need.
Do you find that you spend a significant amount of your time feeling excessively worried or anxious about various aspects of your life, such as your job, your health, or your daily responsibilities?

Well, I wouldn't say I spend a *significant* amount of time worrying, no. I mean, everyone gets a little stressed sometimes, right? Especially in retail, you want things to run smoothly, and you want to do right by your team and the customers. 

But I'm definitely not excessively anxious or anything like that. I try to keep a positive attitude about things. I mean, I worry a normal amount about doing a good job, but it doesn't take over my life or anything. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to reassure you that I'm managing my stress okay, mostly. Is that what you were looking for?
Have you noticed any instances where you have forgotten recent events, lost your keys, or struggled to remember the names of people you know well?

No, no, my memory is actually quite good. I mean, I might occasionally misplace my reading glasses for a minute, but who doesn't do that at my age, right? 

I haven't been forgetting things or losing my keys, and I definitely know everyone's name on my team and the regular customers. I pride myself on that, actually. Being a supervisor, you really have to stay sharp and organized, and I've always been very careful about that. 

So, no memory issues at all. I hope that's what you were hoping to hear? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details so you can figure out what's going on with my speech. Am I doing okay with these questions?

When you say your words get 'tangled up,' is it more that you cannot find the specific word you are looking for, or is it more that your thoughts seem to skip from one topic to another before you finish your original point?

Well, um... I guess it's more the second thing. It's not really that I can't find the word. It's just... well, it's a little embarrassing, honestly. I actually came in because... when I try to explain the inventory numbers to my team, or go over the weekend schedule, my words just start jumping around. 

Like, I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then somehow I'm on to Thursdays, and then... I don't know, the church grill, and then my boss’s tone of voice. And my staff just look at me like they absolutely cannot follow what I’m saying. I try so hard to be a good communicator for my team, so it's a bit shameful to admit that I'm confusing them like that. 

Is that the kind of example you were looking for? I hope I'm making sense to you right now. I really want to be helpful and give you the right answers.
Have you always been someone who tends to jump from topic to topic when you speak, or is this way of communicating a relatively new change for you?

Well, it's... it's definitely a newer thing. I've always prided myself on being very clear and organized, you know, being a supervisor and all. But I guess... well, the jumbled explanations, like when I'm out on the sales floor, and sometimes I just sort of stop mid-sentence... it's been noticeable for about six months now. 

I really tried to just push through it and, you know, not make a big deal out of it. I didn't want anyone to think I couldn't handle my job. But six months is a while, I suppose. I hope it's not too bad that I waited this long to come in? I just wanted to be sure it was a real issue before bothering anyone with it. Does that timeline make sense to you?

Have your colleagues or family members mentioned any other changes in your personality or behavior, such as becoming more irritable, impulsive, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, over these past six months?

Oh, um... no. No, nothing like that. I mean, retail can be a little stressful sometimes, sure, but I definitely haven't been irritable or snapping at anyone. I always try to keep a very positive attitude for my team. I think they'd tell you I'm pretty easy to get along with. 

And I still enjoy all my regular activities—spending time with the family, relaxing on my days off, things like that. Nobody has said anything to me about my personality changing... at least, I really hope they haven't been saying anything like that behind my back. But no, I haven't been impulsive or down or anything. I try to be very even-keeled, especially at work. 

Is that what you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are going. I hope I'm being helpful.
Have you ever been diagnosed by a doctor with any medical conditions, such as a head injury, a stroke, or any other illness that affects your brain?

No, no, nothing like that. I've never had a stroke or a head injury, or anything wrong with my brain. I mean, my health is generally very good. I make sure to take care of myself, you know, getting enough sleep and all that, so I can be at my best for my team. 

I've never been told I have any medical conditions like that. I really try to stay on top of my health. I hope that's a good thing? I mean, it's good that I don't have those things, right? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.

Do you find that you have any unusual beliefs, such as feeling that events around you have a special, personal meaning, or that you have a unique way of interpreting things that others sometimes find strange?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I've always been a very practical person. I mean, you kind of have to be, managing a retail floor and keeping everything running smoothly. I don't really look for hidden meanings in things or... or interpret things in a way that people would find strange. 

I always just try to see everything exactly as it is, very straightforward. I wouldn't want anyone on my team or my family thinking I had bizarre ideas or anything. I hope I haven't given you the impression that I think that way? I really just try to be as level-headed and normal as possible. Does that sound okay to you? I just want to make sure I'm answering correctly.
Have you noticed any subtle changes in the way you walk, such as feeling slightly more unsteady on your feet or having a different rhythm to your stride?

Oh, no, definitely not. I haven't noticed anything like that. I actually spend most of my day on my feet, walking the sales floor and checking on things, so... well, I think I'd definitely notice if I were getting unsteady. Or my team would, and I wouldn't want them worrying about me. 

My stride is just the same as it's always been. I actually try to keep a pretty brisk pace at work so I look energetic and set a good example for the younger staff. I don't want anyone thinking I'm losing my step, you know? 

So, no, everything is very steady. I hope that's a good sign? I mean, it's a good thing that I'm walking fine, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay and giving you the right answers.

When you are speaking to your team and your thoughts jump from one topic to another, are you aware that you are losing your train of thought at the moment it happens, or do you only realize it after someone points it out or looks confused?

Well... I suppose it's more the latter. I don't always catch it right in the moment. I actually came in because... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but when I try to explain things to the staff, like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words just sort of... start jumping around. 

I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then somehow I'm on to Thursdays, and then the church grill, or maybe my boss's tone of voice. In my head, I'm just trying to cover all the bases, but then I see them looking at me like they just can't follow what I'm saying. They get this confused look on their faces, and that's usually when I realize I've lost the thread. 

I just have so much to keep track of on the floor, you know? I really try my best to be clear and professional for them. I hope it's not too unusual to get a little jumbled when you're busy? I mean, everyone gets a little ahead of themselves sometimes, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information here. Am I explaining this okay?

When you are not under the pressure of work or explaining complex tasks to your team, do you find that your thoughts still wander or jump between topics when you are just having a casual, relaxed conversation with a friend or family member?

Oh, um, casual conversations? No, no, I don't think so. When I'm just relaxing, things are... they're much smoother. I mean, I really try to just be present when I'm with my family or talking to a friend. 

It's really just the stress of the store, I think. You know, when you have a million things to manage and everyone is looking at you for directions, it's easy to get a little tongue-tied. But when I'm just sitting down for coffee or chatting with my wife, I... I don't think I jump around like that. I try very hard to just be a good listener and keep things normal. 

I wouldn't want my family thinking I can't hold a simple conversation, you know? So I make sure to just focus on what they're saying. That makes sense, doesn't it? It's pretty normal to only get scattered when you're under pressure, right? I hope I'm making sense.

Looking back at the six-month period when these communication issues began, were there any significant life changes, such as a shift in your job responsibilities, a conflict with your boss, or any personal stressors at home?

Oh, well... actually, if I'm being completely honest, it's been a little longer than six months. I hope you don't mind me correcting you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate timeline so I'm doing this right. 

It's really been building for, oh, about 11 months now. We had a new district manager come in around then, and... well, he just started pushing a lot harder on the sales forecasts and the floor schedules. It's not a bad conflict or anything! I really try to get along with him and do exactly what he asks. It's just... a bit more pressure to perform, I guess. I try so hard to keep up because I want the store to look good and I want him to be happy with my work. 

That's a pretty normal kind of workplace stress, right? I mean, adjusting to a new boss's expectations is an adjustment for anyone. I hope that's the kind of detail you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and answering your questions the right way.
When you are in those moments at work where your thoughts feel jumbled, do you notice any physical sensations like a racing heart, sweating, or a sense of feeling overwhelmed?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really make it a point to keep my composure on the floor. I wouldn't want the staff to see me sweating or... or breathing hard like I'm panicking. That wouldn't be very professional of me as a supervisor, would it? 

So, no, physically, I feel fine. It's just... it's really just the words that get a little tangled up when I'm trying to get all the instructions out at once. I don't feel physically overwhelmed or anything like that. I really try to stay calm and collected for the team so they feel confident in my leadership. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions correctly and giving you what you need.
